M.S. Ramachandra Rao, Chief Justice.

This application is filed by the applicants-Corporation under Section 5 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1963 seeking condonation of delay of 212 days in filing this appeal challenging the judgment dt. 07.11.2022 passed by the learned Single Judge in CWP no.690 of 2008.

2) In the application filed seeking condonation of delay, the delay is incorrectly shown 170 days and it is casually stated that delay in filing the appeal was occasioned only due to the fact that the file for filing the appeal had to be routed through various channels which took considerable time and ultimately, only in the month of June 2023, the present counsel was engaged and asked to file the appeal and the appeal was thus filed on 14.06.2023.
.

sentences.text:
Reply was filed by the respondent, opposing the condonation of delay stating that immediately after the judgment was rendered by the learned Single Judge on 07.11.2022, the respondent had sent copy of the same to the applicants-Corporation by registered post of and thereafter,he had even sent reminders on 11.05.2023 &
13.06.2023.

He stated that when no action was taken on the said rt representations,
he filed COPC no.247 of 2023, and at that point of time, the applicants had informed the Court that the LPA had been filed.
He contended that the delay has not properly been explained by the applicants and they have been negligent in pursuing the legal remedy.
4) We have noted the contentions of the parties.

5) A perusal of the certified copy of the judgment in the Writ petition filed by the applicants,
indicates that though the judgment of the learned Single Judge was rendered on 07.11.2022,
application for certified copy was not made till 23.05.2023, i.e. for almost six months and there is no explanation for this period of delay in making application for certified copy of the impugned judgment.

6) In Postmaster General and others Vs. Living Media India Limited and another,1 the Supreme Court held: -
"25.

entities.text: Postmaster General and others Vs. Living Media India Limited and another,1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
We have already extracted the reasons as mentioned in the "better affidavit"
sworn by Mr. Aparajeet Pattanayak, SSRM, Air .
Mail Sorting Division, New Delhi.

It is relevant to note that in the said affidavit, the Department has itself mentioned and is aware of the date of the judgment of the Division Bench of the High Court in Office of the Chief Postmaster v. Living Media India Ltd. as 11.09.2009.

entities.text: Office of the Chief Postmaster v. Living Media India Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even according to the deponent, their counsel had applied for the certified copy of the said judgment only on 08.01.2010 of and the same was received by the Department on the very same day.
There is no explanation for not applying for certified copy of the impugned judgment on 11.09.2009 or at least within a reasonable rt time.
The fact remains that the certified copy was applied only on 08.01.2010, i.e. after a period of nearly four months.

26. In spite of affording another opportunity to file better affidavit by placing adequate material, neither the Department nor the person in- charge has filed any explanation for not applying the certified copy within the prescribed period.

The other dates mentioned in the affidavit which we have already extracted, clearly show that there was delay at every stage and except mentioning the dates of receipt of the file and the decision taken, there is no explanation as to why such delay had occasioned.

Though it was stated by the Department that the delay was due to unavoidable circumstances and genuine difficulties, the fact remains that from day one the Department or the person/persons concerned have not evinced diligence in prosecuting the matter to this Court by taking appropriate steps.

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that the person(s) concerned were well aware or conversant with the issues involved including the prescribed period of limitation for taking up the matter by way of filing a special leave petition in this Court.
They cannot claim that they have a separate period of limitation when the Department was possessed with competent persons familiar with court proceedings.

In the (2012) 3 SCC 563 absence of plausible and acceptable explanation, we are posing a question why the delay is to be condoned mechanically merely because the Government or a wing of the Government is a party before us.

28. Though we are conscious of the fact that in a matter of .
condonation of delay when there was no gross negligence or deliberate inaction or lack of bona fides,
a liberal concession has to be adopted to advance substantial justice, we are of the view that in the facts and circumstances, the Department cannot take advantage of various earlier decisions.
The claim on account of impersonal machinery and inherited bureaucratic methodology of making several of notes cannot be accepted in view of the modern technologies being used and available.

The law of limitation undoubtedly binds everybody, including the Government."
7) rt

Ltd.3, Union of India vs. Central Tibetan Schools Administration & others4, Union of India & others vs. Vishnu Aroma Pouching Private Limited and another5, and State of Uttar Pradesh & others vs. Sabha Narain & others6.

8) We shall now discuss the judgment cited by the counsel for the applicants:-
(2022) 3 SCC 159 (2022) 2 SCC 327 (2021) 11 SCC 557 (2022) 9 SCC 263 (2022) 9 SCC 266 (a) The decision in Delhi Development Authority Vs. Jagan Singh & Others, Civil Appeal no.4335 of 2023, decided on 13.07.2023.
The said appeal arose out of an order passed by the High .
Court allowing a Writ Petition which had been challenged in the Supreme Court with a delay of 1231 days.

entities.text: Delhi Development Authority Vs. Jagan Singh & Others, Civil Appeal no.4335 of 2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though it was observed by the Supreme Court that the application for condonation of delay was drafted casually in that case, the Bench of had decided to adopt the justice-oriented and liberal approach and condoned the delay.

rt A reading of the said judgment indicates that the Delhi High Court had allowed a Writ petition holding that acquisition proceedings were deemed to have lapsed in view of sub-Section 2 of Section 24 of the 2013 Act, placing reliance on the judgment of the Pune Municipal Corporation & Another Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ... vs Janak Raj & Anr on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29441057/
3 vs. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki & others7.

entities.text: Pune Municipal Corporation & Another Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ... vs Janak Raj & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Afterwards, the said judgment in Pune Municipal Corporation & Another was overruled by the Supreme Court on 06.03.2020 in Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal & others8.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal & others8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Supreme Court, therefore, first decided that the proceedings for acquisition would not lapse;
and that sub-Section (2) of Section 24 of the 2013 Act would have no application because possession of the (2014) 3 SCC 183 (2020) 8 SCC 129 acquired land was already taken on 19.01.2006 though compensation had not been paid.

It therefore condoned the delay as acquired land had already been .
utilized for a public purpose for a Metro Depot.

While observing that it was not influenced by the fact that the decision on which the impugned judgment was based had been overruled and though the SLP had been filed 2 years 3 days after the date of decision of the of Supreme Court in Indore Development Authority (supra-8), it held that the Supreme Court had repeatedly taken a view that liberal and rt justice-oriented approach needs to be adopted in the matters of condonation of delay,
so that substantive rights of parties are not defeated only on the ground of delay.

We may point out that the decision in Postmaster General and others (supra-1) and the other judgments referred to above applying it have neither been adverted to nor considered and applied by the Supreme Court in the above case.
May be in the facts & circumstances in Delhi Development Authority, the Supreme Court thought it fit to condone the delay.
However, we prefer to follow the judgment in Postmaster General and others (supra-1) and the other cases which followed it.

(b) The next judgment cited by the counsel for the applicants is decision of the Supreme Court rendered on 24.07.2023 in Civil Appeal no.4628 of 2023.
.
In this case the delay was only 52 days in filing the appeal.

So the Court observed that parties were litigating with regard to rights over immovable property and substantive rights were to be decided between the parties, and the High Court was in error in refusing to of condone the said period of delay in filing the first appeal before the Appellate Court.
Also, in that case neither the State nor an rt instrumentality of the State was a party.
Thus the said decision is distinguishable and it cannot be applied to the instant case since the delay on its part is 212 days, for which no valid reason has been furnished by the applicants.

(c) Counsel for the applicants relied on the judgment of the Supreme Court in Sheo Raj Singh (deceased) through LRs & Others Vs. Union of India & Another, Civil Appeal no.5867 of 2015 dt.

sentences.text: In Sheo Raj Singh, the High Court had condoned the delay of 479 days in filing a Land Acquisition Appeal in the High Court and the explanation offered found favour with the Supreme Court.

In that case, the Supreme Court observed that it was not hearing an application for condonation of delay,
but was sitting in appeal over discretionary exercise of the High Court granting the prayer for condonation of delay; in the case of the former, whether to condone or not, would be the only question, whereas in the .
latter, whether there has been proper exercise of discretion in favour of grant of prayer for condonation, would be the question;
and the law was well settled that a Court of appeal should not ordinarily interfere with the discretionary exercise by the Courts of below, and that the appellate power should be exercised only when the order challenged in appeal is clearly wrong and not when it is rt merely not right.

The said decision therefore cannot help the applicants since in the instant application, this Court has to consider the question whether sufficient cause has been shown to condone the period of delay.
It is not considering an order passed by a subordinate forum condoning the delay or refusing to condone it.

9) Having regard to the law declared by the Supreme Court in Postmaster General (supra-1) and the other decisions which followed it, and also taking into account the fact that the respondent is now aged 64 years, and it would be not in the interest of justice to compel him at this stage of his life to contest this litigation, and since no sufficient cause for condonation of delay has been given by the applicants, this application is dismissed.
10) Consequently, the appeal (Filing No.LPA/16171/2023), is also .
dismissed.
11) Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
(M.S. Ramachandra Rao)
